## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Suddhaṭṭhakasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 4) is the fourth chapter of the *Mahāniddesa*, the first book of the canonical commentary *Niddesa* in the Khuddaka Nikāya of the Pali Sutta Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The text serves as an extensive prose commentary and word-by-word exposition on the *Suddhaṭṭhaka Sutta* (the "Octad on Purity" from the Aṭṭhakavagga) [SuttaCentral]. Two modern translations in two languages are registered on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral].

Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral connect passages of the *Suddhaṭṭhakasuttaniddesa* to other Niddesa texts, namely the *Pasūrasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 8) and the *Nandamāṇavapucchāniddesa* (Cnd 11), as well as to Abhidhamma treatises in the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī* (Ds 2.3.2 *Dukanikkhepa* and Ds 2.4.2 *Dukaatthuddhāra*) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus computational text-reuse analysis confirms these relationships, recording substantial shared segments between Mnd 4 and Cnd 11 (e.g. §47.3_1–53.1 ↔ §10.2_4–14.1) as well as Mnd 8 (e.g. §13.5–13.14 ↔ §3.3–3.12) [DharmaNexus].

Beyond these curated parallels, DharmaNexus reports extensive Pali-internal formulaic reuse amounting to 2,980 matching passages across 127 Pali texts, reflecting the standardized exegetical vocabulary of the *Niddesa* tradition [DharmaNexus]. The largest reuse partners within the *Mahāniddesa* include the *Mahābyūhasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 13; over 20,000 shared characters), the *Māgaṇḍiyasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 9), the *Purābhedasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 10), the *Duṭṭhaṭṭhakasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 3), and the *Paramaṭṭhakasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 5), along with canonical doctrinal passages shared with the *Nidāna Saṁyutta* (SN 12) and the *Paṭiccasamuppādavibhaṅga* (Vb 6) [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, DharmaNexus identifies automatic cross-language alignments with Sanskrit and Tibetan canonical and philosophical texts—including the *Saṅghabhedavastu*, the *Arthaviniścayasūtra*, Candrakīrti's *Prasannapadā*, the *Śālistambasūtra*, the *Abhiniṣkramaṇa-sūtra*, and the *Karmaśataka*—primarily matching standardized doctrinal sequences such as dependent origination (§42.6–42.8) [DharmaNexus].
